meta.title: The Color That Sets the Order
meta.skill_frame: Process: order the work by the setup it shares, not by when it arrived.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 6.29, 6.28 and 5.90 on the three parts (131, 118 and 106 words), 6.16 together. The load is one trade: the board groups jobs by ink to save setup time, and a due time can break the grouping, so the reader must hold the cost and the order at once.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for process 4.3, band 4.3, sequence 1. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A small print shop running four jobs in two inks on one press, ordered by ink changes and bounded by a noon delivery.
source.avoided: No shop name, city, press brand, wage, or price. No claim about how many jobs a day the shop takes.

session.difficulty_basis: The order is chosen by what the steps share, and that choice has a cost that arrives from outside the work.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A small print shop runs four jobs on one press in a single afternoon. Two of the jobs print in blue ink and two print in green. Changing ink is slow work. The press has to be washed down, the rollers cleaned, and the first sheets thrown away until the color runs even. A wash-up takes about twenty minutes and wastes a few sheets of heavy paper. The foreman writes the schedule on a board beside the press. She does not write the jobs down in the order the customers sent them, and she does not start with the job that has waited longest. She writes them in the order that needs the fewest ink changes, because that order decides how much of the afternoon the press spends standing still.
passage.part_2: Four jobs in two colors need two wash-ups if each color runs together. Taken in the order they arrived, the same four jobs can need three, and each wash-up costs twenty minutes and a few sheets. The grouping therefore saves the shop most of an hour of press time. The saving is not free. A job that arrived first can wait behind a later job of the same color, and the customer on the telephone does not care about ink. The noon delivery decides which group runs first, so the greens run first and the blues wait. A late delivery costs the shop more than a wash-up costs, which is the trade the board records.
passage.part_3: The order on the board follows the setup, not the day the job came in. That is the rule, and it carries one condition. A wash-up can be avoided, but a due time cannot be moved, so the due time outranks the color when the two disagree. The foreman checks two things before writing the board: which jobs share an ink, and which group is due first. Everything else is free to move. A shop that sorts by arrival instead pays for both, in extra wash-ups and in late jobs. The board is rewritten every afternoon, because the jobs and their due times change.

items.prompt: In what order does the foreman write the jobs on the board?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. In the order that needs the fewest ink changes.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says she writes them in the order that needs the fewest ink changes, not in the order they arrived.
tutor_only.tell: The foreman sorts the jobs by ink. She writes the order that needs the fewest changes.
help: The sentence about the board says which order the foreman writes down.
It is the order that keeps the press from being washed down between jobs.
tutor_only.core_idea: The order that needs the fewest ink changes.
accept_ideas: the order with the fewest ink changes
sorted so the same color runs together
the order that needs the fewest wash-ups
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the order the customers sent the jobs
if_they_say.ask: The passage says she does not use that order. What does she use instead?

items.prompt: Four jobs in two colors need two wash-ups when each color runs together. Why can the same jobs in arrival order need three?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Arrival order can switch ink back and forth.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the same four jobs can need three wash-ups when taken in the order they arrived, because the ink keeps changing.
tutor_only.tell: Arrival order can put a blue job between two greens. Every switch costs a wash-up.
help: The sentence about the same four jobs in arrival order gives the number three.
Each switch of ink costs a wash-up, so alternating colors cost more.
tutor_only.core_idea: Arrival order alternates the inks, so more switches are needed.
accept_ideas: the colors alternate, so each change costs a wash-up
arrival order switches ink more often
it breaks the colors up into more changes
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says arrival order is slower because of the paper
if_they_say.ask: Paper is wasted at every wash-up. What makes more wash-ups happen?

items.prompt: The greens run first even though the blues arrived first. Why?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The greens are due at noon.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the noon delivery decides which group runs first, and a late delivery costs more than a wash-up.
tutor_only.tell: A due time beats the arrival date. The greens are due at noon, so they run first.
help: The sentence about the noon delivery says which group runs first.
One group has a time on it that the shop cannot move.
tutor_only.core_idea: The greens are due at noon, and a late delivery costs more than a wash-up.
accept_ideas: the noon deadline outranks the earlier arrival
a late delivery costs more than a wash-up
the greens have to go out by noon
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the greens came in first
if_they_say.ask: The blues arrived first. What does the green group have that the blues do not?

items.prompt: A blue job due at four arrives after the green job due at noon. Where does it go on the board, and why?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. With the other blues, after the greens.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The blues share an ink, and the noon green group is due first, so the new blue joins its color group behind the greens.
tutor_only.tell: It goes with the blues, behind the greens. The noon job is due first, and the blues still share one wash-up.
help: The passage gives two checks the foreman makes before writing the board.
Shared ink sets the group, and the earliest due time sets which group goes first.
tutor_only.core_idea: With the other blues, after the greens, because the greens are due first and the blues share an ink.
accept_ideas: after the greens, with the other blues
in the blue group, behind the noon job
it joins the blues once the greens are done
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says it goes at the end because it arrived last
if_they_say.ask: Arrival order was already set aside once. What two things set this board?

items.prompt: What decides the order on the board, and what one thing can overrule it?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Shared ink decides it, and an earlier due time overrules it.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the order follows the setup, that a due time outranks the color, and that everything else is free to move.
tutor_only.tell: Shared ink decides the order. An earlier due time overrules the grouping.
help: The passage states the rule and then the condition that outranks it.
One rule is about the press, and the other is about the customer.
tutor_only.core_idea: Shared ink decides the order, and an earlier due time can overrule it.
accept_ideas: the setup decides, and a due time outranks it
grouping by ink, unless a deadline is earlier
ink changes set the order, and a sooner deadline breaks it
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the customer always decides
if_they_say.ask: A due time matters, but what is the order built on first?
